4. As per prosecution story, the applicant alongwith other named co-accused persons is stated to have duped the first informant to the tune of Rs.12,61,000/- on the pretext that his son shall be appointed as Sub Inspector in U.P. Police.
The son of the informant appeared in the entrance examination but failed.
Subsequent to it, a fake appointment letter is stated to have been given to the informant by the co-accused person Jitendra Baitha at Lucknow.
The applicant has duped him of his hard earned money and not got his son appointed as Sub Inspector.

5. Learned counsel for the applicant has argued that the applicant is absolutely innocent and has been falsely implicated in the present case with a view to cause unnecessary harassment and to victimize him.
He has nothing to do with the said offence.
The main accused is Jitendra Baitha and his wife Seema Devi.
The money, if any, has been transferred to the joint account of co-accused person Jitendra Baitha and his wife Seema Devi.
Several other submissions have been made on behalf of the applicant to demonstrate the falsity of the allegations made against him.
The circumstances which, as per counsel, led to the false implication of the applicant have also been touched upon at length.
There is no criminal history of the applicant.
The applicant is languishing in jail since 10.10.2023.
In case, the applicant is released on bail, he will not misuse the liberty of bail.
6. Learned A.G.A. has vehemently opposed the bail application.

7. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, submissions made by learned counsel for the parties, the evidence on record, and without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the Court is of the view that the applicant has made out a case for bail.
The bail application is allowed.

8. Let the applicant-Ori Ahir Alias Ori Prasad Yadav, who is involved in aforementioned case crime be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following conditions.
Further, before issuing the release order, the sureties be verified.
(i) The applicant shall not tamper with evidence.
(ii) The applicant shall remain present, in person, before the Trial Court on dates fixed for (1) opening of the case, (2) framing of charge and (3) recording of statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C.

If in the opinion of the Trial Court absence of the applicant is deliberate or without sufficient cause, then it shall be open for the Trial Court to treat such default as abuse of liberty of bail and proceed against him in accordance with law.
9. In case of breach of any of the above conditions, it shall be a ground for cancellation of bail.

10. It is made clear that observations made in granting bail to the applicant shall not in any way affect the learned trial Judge in forming his independent opinion based on the testimony of the witnesses.

Order Date :- 17.01.2024 Ravi Kant (Krishan Pahal, J.)
